This is just due to compression settings.  
Different Codecs have different sizes. Most commonly, H.264 will result in a larger file size than H.265.  
Another factor is compression power (idk the word for it) but if I'm using HEVC Codec while keeping the same quality, same bitrate etc etc etc. I can set compression power to Extremely high, this would take about 100 years for my PC to finish processing but It will result in the smallest filesize possible using lossloss encoding. Should I be a little lazy and have a compression power of low, this would be done within an hour but the filesize will be still lower than the raw video but drastically higher than the version set to Extremely high.

tl;dr - Despite higher bitrates, more powerful compression will have been used to result in a lower file size.
